subproblem.title: Zero-scale limits of blow-ups of codimension-one boundaries with moving centres are boundaries of regions in offset planes (Simon 7.5.3–7.5.5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ U, points x_i → x of ℝ^P, scales λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume U is open, InClassO n U N ξ_N, E is measurable with E ⊆ N ∩ U, T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(y)(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N), and (a) there are C ∈ ℝ and r₀ > 0 with M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Cρ^n) (T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C·ρ^n)) for all y ∈ B_{r₀}(x) and 0 < ρ < r₀; (b) the blow-ups η_{x_i,λ_i#}T (blowUp T x_i λ_i, η_{y,λ}(w) = λ^{−1}(w − y)) converge weakly to S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (c) spt S ≠ ∅. Then there are a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with dim Q = n + 1, a ∈ ℝ^P, a Borel set F ⊆ ℝ^P and ξ_A ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) such that, with A := {y : y + a ∈ Q} = Q − a: InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ_A) (A is an affine (n+1)-plane in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P, oriented by the constant ξ_A); F ⊆ A; and S = ∂[[F]] in ℝ^P, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_F ξ_A(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) (IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_A)).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 3 (C2(ii)) of the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity, departure [D4]: zero-scale limits of blow-ups with moving centres are boundaries of regions in offset tangent planes. This is the codimension-one compactness argument of Simon 7.5.3–7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901), using the BV compactness theorem Ch. 2, 2.6 (chapter-02.txt lines 598–625) and lower semicontinuity of the variation (Ch. 2, §2; SimonGMT Chapter02.bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1). It is part A2 of the previously reviewed analytic core of this node, with these changes: the hypotheses on T are only those used (no minimality of T, and no hypothesis on S other than nonempty support); the conclusion stops at S = ∂[[F]] in the offset plane A = Q − a, which lies in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P. The parent then applies the sibling children region_support_cycle and region_density_one to S (U := ℝ^P, N := A, E := F) to get spt S ⊆ A and dense density-one points, exactly as the supplied step 3 ends with “as in step 1 with N replaced by A”. The linear inclusion of parent step 4 (0 ∈ spt S forces a ∈ Q) is also left to the parent.
Departure from parent step 3(α): the uniform local mass bound (a) is a hypothesis, replacing the monotonicity constant “Λ for K := closedBall x (2δ₀)”; the parent supplies (a) from the sibling monotonicity (i).

Sibling children used (accepted declarations, reused with their identical frozen types).
- hausdorff_dilation (Submission.dtc_hausdorff_dilation): for x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and d ∈ ℕ, Measure.map (dilation x λ) μHE[d] = ofReal(λ^d)·μHE[d] (part (ii)).
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): a continuous linear L : Λ_k → Λ^k with |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, |L(ξ)| ≤ 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = 1 for every unit orientation ξ of a subspace.
- orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg): two unit orientations of the same subspace satisfy w = v or w = −v.

Notation.
- H^d := μHE[d]; on a d-dimensional affine plane it is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. ω_d := unitBallVolume d. B_ρ(y) := ball y ρ. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector; M_W(T) := T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ 1 pointwise (admissible ω).
- “T vanishes on W” means T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W; spt T := U ∖ Z(T), Z(T) the union of the open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes.
- η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (dilation y λ). blowUp T y λ = η_{y,λ#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{y,λ}(U)) acts by η_{y,λ#}T(ω) = T(η_{y,λ}^#ω).
- S_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly) means currentEval(S_i)(ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω) if tsupport ω lies in the domain of S_i, and 0 otherwise.

Lemma (A-plane: affine planes with a constant unit orientation lie in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P). Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace and ξ ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, let a ∈ ℝ^P, and put A := {y : y + a ∈ Q}. Then InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ).
1. Choose τ : Fin(n+1) → ℝ^P orthonormal with span τ = Q. Put ι(v) := Σ_i v_iτ_i and ψ(v) := ι(v) − a for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. |ι(v)|² = Σ_i v_i², so ι is an injective linear isometry with range Q (and dim Q = n + 1); ψ(ℝ^{n+1}) = A.
2. Embedded chart. For y ∈ A take V := ℝ^{n+1}, W := ℝ^P and the chart ψ: ψ is affine, hence C^∞; it is injective with ψ(V) = W ∩ A; Dψ = ι is injective; for compact K, ψ^{−1}(K) is closed and bounded (|v| = |ψ(v) + a| ≤ max_K|·| + |a|), hence compact. So IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) A.
3. A is the preimage of the closed subspace Q under y ↦ y + a, so closure A = A and (closure A ∖ A) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅. Also −a ∈ A, so A ∩ ℝ^P ≠ ∅.
4. tangentSpace(A, y) = Q for y ∈ A: if γ is C¹ with values in A and γ(0) = y, then t^{−1}(γ(t) − γ(0)) ∈ Q and Q is closed, so γ'(0) ∈ Q; conversely for v ∈ Q the curve γ(t) := y + tv lies in A with γ'(0) = v.
5. The constant map y ↦ ξ is continuous and is a unit orientation of Q = tangentSpace(A, y) at every y ∈ A; so IsOrientation (n+1) A (y ↦ ξ).
Steps 2–5 are the four conjuncts of InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ).

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement; write (a) for the mass bound with constants C, r₀, (b) for S_i ⇀ S, and (d) for spt S ≠ ∅.
Set-up. Put η_i := η_{x_i,λ_i}, S_i := η_{i#}T and c_* := max{C, 0}. Passing to a subsequence is harmless throughout: S is the weak limit of every subsequence, and x_i → x, λ_i → 0 persist. Fix δ₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2δ₀) ⊆ U. For i large (|x_i − x| < δ₀), B_{δ₀}(x_i) ⊆ U, hence η_i(U) ⊇ B_{δ₀/λ_i}(0).
1. (Representation of S_i.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U).
- S_i(ω) = T(η_i^#ω), where η_i^#ω is the affine pull-back (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm with linear part λ_i^{−1}I and translation −λ_i^{−1}x_i), because blowUp is the affinePushforward of T restricted to η_i^{−1}(η_i(U)) = U. Its tsupport is η_i^{−1}(tsupport ω) ⊆ U. By multilinearity, (η_i^#β)(y) = λ_i^{−j}β(η_i(y)) for every j-form β.
- d commutes with affine pull-back (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), so d(η_i^#ω) = η_i^#(dω) = λ_i^{−(n+1)}(dω)∘η_i, and S_i(ω) = ∫_E λ_i^{−(n+1)} ξ_N(y)(dω(η_i(y))) dH^{n+1}(y).
- Change of variables. η_i is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse w ↦ x_i + λ_iw, and by hausdorff_dilation (ii) in dimension n + 1, η_{i#}H^{n+1} = λ_i^{n+1}H^{n+1}. Hence ∫ f(η_i(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) = λ_i^{n+1}∫ f dH^{n+1} for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ; this identity of Bochner integrals needs no integrability assumption (integration along the measurable equivalence η_i, Mathlib integral_map_equiv, then integral_smul_measure).
- Apply it to f(w) := 1_{E_i}(w)·λ_i^{−(n+1)}ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw)(dω(w)), E_i := η_i(E): since y ∈ E ⟺ η_i(y) ∈ E_i and x_i + λ_iη_i(y) = y, with ξ_i(w) := ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw) we get
 S_i(ω) = ∫_{E_i} ξ_i(w)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w).
- Put N_i := η_i(N). If ω vanishes on an open set O' containing E_i ∩ tsupport ω (in particular if tsupport ω ∩ N_i = ∅), then S_i(ω) = 0, since dω = 0 on O' and off tsupport ω.
2. (Uniform mass bounds from (a).)
(2a) Let W be open with η_i^{−1}(W) ⊆ U and ω admissible for M_W(S_i). Then (η_i^#ω)(y) = λ_i^{−n}ω(η_i(y)), so λ_i^nη_i^#ω is admissible for M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T) (pointwise norm ≤ 1, tsupport a compact subset of η_i^{−1}(W) ⊆ U). Hence S_i(ω) = λ_i^{−n}T(λ_i^nη_i^#ω) ≤ λ_i^{−n}M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T), i.e. M_W(S_i) ≤ λ_i^{−n}M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T).
(2b) For W := B_ρ(0), η_i^{−1}(W) = B_{λ_iρ}(x_i). If x_i ∈ B_{r₀}(x), λ_iρ < r₀ and B_{λ_iρ}(x_i) ⊆ U, then (a) gives M_{B_ρ(0)}(S_i) ≤ λ_i^{−n}·c_*(λ_iρ)^n = c_*ρ^n.
3. (dist(x_i, N) = O(λ_i), and x ∈ N.) N ≠ ∅ since N ∩ U ≠ ∅. Suppose dist(x_i, N)/λ_i were unbounded; pass to a subsequence with dist(x_i, N)/λ_i → ∞, so dist(0, N_i) = dist(x_i, N)/λ_i → ∞. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0). For large i, tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U), so currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω), and B_R(0) ∩ N_i = ∅, so S_i(ω) = 0 by step 1. Hence S(ω) = 0 for every ω, S vanishes on every ball, and spt S = ∅, contradicting (d). So there is C₀ ≥ 1 with dist(x_i, N) ≤ C₀λ_i for all i. Letting i → ∞, dist(x, N) = 0, so x ∈ closure(N) ∩ U ⊆ N because (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅.
4. (Graph chart of N at x; parent 3(β).)
(4a) Tangent plane. IsOrientation (n+1) N ξ_N at x gives a subspace Π₀ with Π₀ = tangentSpace(N, x) and IsUnitOrientationOf(ξ_N(x), Π₀); dim Π₀ = n + 1. Put ξ_A := ξ_N(x), p := orthogonal projection onto Π₀, p^⊥ := I − p.
(4b) Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at x (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N) and z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x. ψ : V → W ∩ N is a continuous bijection with V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W; such a map is closed into the locally compact Hausdorff space W, so W ∩ N = ψ(V) is closed in W and ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ N. For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and small ε > 0, t ↦ ψ(z₀ + εtv) is a C¹ curve in N through x with velocity εDψ(z₀)v, so range Dψ(z₀) ⊆ Π₀; Dψ(z₀) is injective and dim Π₀ = n + 1, so range Dψ(z₀) = Π₀.
(4c) By the inverse function theorem p∘(ψ − x) is a C² diffeomorphism of an open V₀ ∋ z₀ onto an open neighbourhood O of 0 in Π₀; ψ(V₀) ⊇ N ∩ B_s(x) for some s > 0 (ψ(V₀) is relatively open in W ∩ N). Put u := p^⊥∘(ψ − x)∘(p∘(ψ − x)|_{V₀})^{−1} : O → Π₀^⊥, a C² map with u(0) = 0 and Du(0) = 0. Choose r₁ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x), δ₂ := r₁, and δ₁ ∈ (0, r₁) with D := Π₀ ∩ B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ O, |Du| ≤ 1 on D and |u| < δ₂/2 on D. The open cylinder Z := {x + v + h : v ∈ Π₀, |v| < δ₁, h ∈ Π₀^⊥, |h| < δ₂} has compact closure inside U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x).
(4d) Put Γ(v) := x + v + u(v) for v ∈ D. Then N ∩ Z = Γ(D) (a point q ∈ N ∩ Z lies in ψ(V₀), so v := p(q − x) ∈ D and q = Γ(v); conversely Γ(D) ⊆ N ∩ Z). Γ is an injective C² map with DΓ(v) = I + Du(v) on Π₀, and tangentSpace(N, Γ(v)) = DΓ(v)Π₀ (curves t ↦ Γ(v + εtw), and every C¹ curve γ in N through Γ(v) equals Γ∘(p∘(γ − x)) near t = 0).
(4e) Orientation formula. For v ∈ D let J(v) := det(DΓ(v)τ_i·DΓ(v)τ_j)^{1/2} > 0 for an orthonormal basis τ of Π₀ with ξ_A(β) = ±β(τ), and η(v)(α) := ξ_A(α(DΓ(v)·, …, DΓ(v)·))/J(v). Gram–Schmidt (DΓ(v)τ = σU, σ orthonormal, U upper triangular with positive diagonal, det U = J(v)) shows that η(v) is a unit orientation of DΓ(v)Π₀ = tangentSpace(N, Γ(v)). So is ξ_N(Γ(v)) (IsOrientation); by orientation_sign, ξ_N(Γ(v)) = s(v)η(v) with s(v) ∈ {±1}. With L from unit_orientation_dual, s(v) = ξ_N(Γ(v))(L(η(v))) is continuous on the connected set D (ξ_N continuous on N; Γ, DΓ, J continuous; L continuous), and s(0) = 1 because η(0) = ξ_A = ξ_N(x). Hence
 ξ_N(x + v + u(v)) = η(v) = Λ_{n+1}(I + Du(v))ξ_A/J(v) for all v ∈ D.
(4f) Rescaled graphs. Write x_i − x = s_i + t_i with s_i ∈ Π₀ and t_i ∈ Π₀^⊥; then s_i, t_i → 0. Put dom G_i := {w ∈ Π₀ : |s_i + λ_iw| < δ₁}, g_i(w) := λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i) ∈ Π₀^⊥ and G_i(w) := w + g_i(w). Then:
- η_i(x + v + u(v)) = G_i(λ_i^{−1}(v − s_i)), so η_i(N ∩ Z) = G_i(dom G_i);
- p∘G_i = id and p^⊥∘G_i = g_i; G_i is injective;
- DG_i(w) = I + Du(s_i + λ_iw) on Π₀, so Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) and |Dg_i| ≤ 1;
- x_i + λ_iG_i(w) = Γ(s_i + λ_iw), so by (4e) ξ_i(G_i(w)) = Λ_{n+1}DG_i(w)ξ_A/J_i(w), where J_i(w) := J(s_i + λ_iw) is the Jacobian of G_i.
5. (Offset; parent 3(γ).)
- Choose p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ 2C₀λ_i. Then p_i → x, so for large i, p_i ∈ Z and p_i = x + v_i + u(v_i) with v_i ∈ D.
- w_i := λ_i^{−1}(v_i − s_i) ∈ dom G_i satisfies G_i(w_i) = η_i(p_i), and |η_i(p_i)| = |p_i − x_i|/λ_i ≤ 2C₀. Hence |w_i| = |p(G_i(w_i))| ≤ 2C₀ and |g_i(w_i)| ≤ 2C₀.
- For large i, dom G_i is convex and contains 0 and w_i, and |Dg_i| ≤ 1, so |g_i(0)| ≤ |g_i(w_i)| + |w_i| ≤ 4C₀.
- Pass to a subsequence with g_i(0) → −a, where a ∈ Π₀^⊥.
- Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) → Du(0) = 0 uniformly for w in bounded sets. So g_i → −a and G_i → G, G(w) := w − a, in C¹ on Π₀ ∩ closedBall(0, R') for every R'.
- Put A := G(Π₀) = Π₀ − a = {y : y + a ∈ Π₀}.
6. (Local geometry; parent 3(δ).) Fix R ≥ 1, R₁ := R + |a| + 2 and C_R := {y : |p(y)| < R, |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 1} ⊆ B_{R₁}(0). For all large i:
- B_{λ_iR₁}(x_i) ⊆ Z and B_{R₁}(0) ⊆ η_i(U);
- x_i ∈ B_{r₀}(x) and λ_iR₁ < r₀;
- Π₀ ∩ closedBall(0, R₁) ⊆ dom G_i, and |g_i(w) + a| < 1/4 for |w| ≤ R₁.
For these i:
(6a) N_i ∩ B_{R₁}(0) = η_i(N ∩ B_{λ_iR₁}(x_i)) ⊆ η_i(N ∩ Z) = G_i(dom G_i).
(6b) N_i ∩ C_R = G_i(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)): a point y of the left side lies in B_{R₁}(0), hence y = G_i(w) with |w| = |p(y)| < R; conversely, for |w| < R, |p(G_i(w))| = |w| < R and |p^⊥(G_i(w))| = |g_i(w)| < |a| + 1/4, and G_i(w) ∈ η_i(N ∩ Z) ⊆ N_i.
(6c) N_i ∩ B_R(0) ⊆ G_i(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)) ⊆ {y : |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 1/4}.
(6d) By (2b), M_{B_{R₁}(0)}(S_i) ≤ c_*R₁^n.
7. (Projected-current identity; parent 3(ε).) Let F_i' := {w ∈ dom G_i : G_i(w) ∈ E_i}, a Borel set, and F_i := G(F_i') = F_i' − a ⊆ A.
(7a) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ C_R, and let i be large. E_i ⊆ N_i, so by (6b) E_i ∩ C_R = G_i(F_i' ∩ B_R(0)). Step 1, the area formula for the injective C¹ map G_i on Π₀ ∩ B_R(0) and (4f) give
 S_i(ω) = ∫_{E_i∩C_R} ξ_i(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A((G_i^#dω)(w)) dH^{n+1}(w).
(7b) Put π_A := G∘p = p − a. Let ζ(y) := χ(|p^⊥(y)|), where χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ; [0, 1]) is 1 on (−∞, |a| + 3/4] and 0 on [|a| + 7/8, ∞); ζ is smooth since χ is constant near 0.
(7c) Let α̃ be a smooth n-form on the plane A with compact support in A ∩ B_R(−a) = G(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)), and put ω := ζ·π_A^#α̃. Then ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ C_R, and on Π₀ ∩ B_R(0) we have π_A∘G_i = G and ζ∘G_i = χ(|g_i|) = 1 (|g_i| < |a| + 1/4), so G_i^#ω = G^#α̃ there. Hence S_i(ω) = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G^#dα̃) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F_i} ξ_A(dα̃) dH^{n+1}, since G is a translation.
8. (Uniform perimeter bound; parent 3(ζ).) If moreover |α̃| ≤ 1, then |ζπ_A^#α̃| ≤ 1: in an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P whose first n + 1 vectors span Π₀, the coefficients of ζπ_A^#α̃ are ζ times those of α̃ and 0 otherwise, and the Euclidean coefficient norm does not depend on the orthonormal basis (coefficients transform by the n-th compound C_n(O) of the orthogonal change of basis O, and C_n(O)C_n(O)ᵀ = I by Cauchy–Binet). So ∫_{F_i} ξ_A(dα̃) dH^{n+1} = S_i(ω) ≤ M_{C_R}(S_i) ≤ M_{B_{R₁}(0)}(S_i) ≤ c_*R₁^n by (6d). Identify A with ℝ^{n+1} by an affine isometry carrying ξ_A to e_1∧⋯∧e_{n+1}; n-forms α̃ with |α̃| ≤ 1 correspond to vector fields φ with |φ| ≤ 1, and ξ_A(dα̃) = div φ. Hence |D1_{F_i}|(A ∩ B_R(−a)) ≤ c_*(R + |a| + 2)^n for all large i ≥ i_R (smooth fields suffice, by mollification), and H^{n+1}(F_i ∩ B_R(−a)) ≤ ω_{n+1}R^{n+1}.
9. (BV compactness; parent 3(η).) For R = 1, 2, … in turn, apply the BV compactness theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 2.6) on the ball A ∩ B_{R+1}(−a) to the tail i ≥ i_{R+1} of the current subsequence; a diagonal subsequence gives f ∈ L¹_loc(A) with 1_{F_i} → f in L¹(A ∩ B_R(−a)) for every R. A further subsequence converges H^{n+1}-a.e. on A. Put F := {y ∈ A : 1_{F_i}(y) → 1}. Then F is Borel, F ⊆ A, 1_F = f H^{n+1}-a.e. on A, and 1_{F_i} → 1_F in L¹(A ∩ B_R(−a)) for every R. (F has locally finite perimeter in A by lower semicontinuity of the variation; this is not needed below.)
10. (Identification of S; parent 3(θ).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). Choose R ∈ ℕ, R ≥ 1, with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0), and write ω = ζω + (1 − ζ)ω.
(10a) (1 − ζ)ω vanishes on the open set O := {y : |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 3/4}. For large i, O ⊇ N_i ∩ B_R(0) ⊇ E_i ∩ tsupport ω by (6c), so S_i((1 − ζ)ω) = 0 by step 1. Also O ⊇ A, because |p^⊥(y)| = |a| for y ∈ A (a ∈ Π₀^⊥); so d((1 − ζ)ω) = 0 on A and ∫_F ξ_A(d((1 − ζ)ω)) dH^{n+1} = 0.
(10b) tsupport(ζω) ⊆ B_R(0) ∩ {|p^⊥| ≤ |a| + 7/8} ⊆ C_R. By (7a), S_i(ζω) = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G_i^#d(ζω)) dH^{n+1}. Here 1_{F_i'} = 1_{F_i}∘G → 1_F∘G in L¹(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)), and G_i^#d(ζω) → G^#d(ζω) uniformly on Π₀ ∩ closedBall(0, R) (G_i → G in C¹). So S_i(ζω) → ∫_{G^{−1}(F)∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G^#d(ζω)) dH^{n+1} = ∫_F ξ_A(d(ζω)) dH^{n+1}.
(10c) For large i, currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω). By (b), S(ω) = lim S_i(ω) = ∫_F ξ_A(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y).
So S(ω) = ∫_F ξ_A(dω) dH^{n+1} for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), i.e. IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_A).
11. (Conclusion.) Put Q := Π₀ and take a from step 5 and F from step 9, with ξ_A = ξ_N(x).
- Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1 by (4a).
- IsUnitOrientationOf(ξ_A, Q) by (4a), so by Lemma A-plane, InClassO n ℝ^P {y : y + a ∈ Q} (y ↦ ξ_A).
- F is Borel (MeasurableSet F) and F ⊆ A = {y : y + a ∈ Q}.
- IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_A) by step 10.
These are the five conjuncts of the conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: The blow-ups are rescaled region boundaries S_i(ω) = ∫_{η_i(E)} ξ_N(x_i + λ_i·)(dω) (change of variables by hausdorff_dilation (ii)), and (a) bounds M_{B_ρ(0)}(S_i) ≤ c_*ρ^n.
spt S ≠ ∅ forces dist(x_i, N) = O(λ_i), hence x ∈ N; in the graph chart of N at x, the rescaled graphs G_i(w) = w + g_i(w) converge in C¹ to the translation w ↦ w − a with a ∈ (T_xN)^⊥.
The projected-current identity ∂[[F_i]] = π_{A#}(ζS_i) on A ∩ B_R(−a) and the mass bound give uniform perimeter bounds for F_i ⊆ A = T_xN − a; BV compactness gives F ⊆ A with 1_{F_i} → 1_F in L¹_loc.
Splitting test forms by the cut-off ζ identifies S = ∂[[F]] in ℝ^P; the offset plane A with constant orientation ξ_N(x) is in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P (Lemma A-plane).

audit.reason: The proof uses only the stated local mass bound and weak convergence. Nonempty limiting support bounds the normal offsets; graph convergence, the projected-current identity and perimeter bounds precede BV compactness. The final test-form limit establishes the exact Borel-region boundary conclusion in an oriented offset plane.
